This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the Seven Creeks to Euroa.
This update includes revised increased flood levels at the Seven Creeks at Euroa and the Seven Creeks downstream of Euroa.

MODERATE FLOODING OCCURRING AT EUROA AND POSSIBLE AT KIALLA WEST FROM MONDAY EVENING
MINOR FLOODING OCCURRING AT STRATHBOGIE, GALLS GAP ROAD AND TELFORDS BRIDGE

  • Rainfall across the Seven and Castle Creeks catchments since Sunday morning has resulted in creek level rises and Moderate flooding. 
  • Rainfall is forecast to continue until Monday afternoon, which may result in further creek level rises and areas of flooding across the Seven and Castle Creeks catchments.
  • The situation is being closely monitored, and this warning will be updated as required.
  • A Flood Watch is still current for many parts of North East Victoria.

Seven Creeks to Euroa
  • Minor flooding is occurring along the Seven Creeks at Strathbogie and Galls Gap Road and Moderate flooding is occurring at Euroa.
  • The Seven Creeks at Euroa is currently at 4.42 metres and rising, with Moderate flooding. 
  • The Seven Creeks at Euroa may peak near 4.50 metres Monday afternoon, with Moderate flooding.
Seven Creeks Downstream of Euroa
  • Moderate flooding is possible along the Seven Creeks at Kialla West.
  • The Seven Creeks at Kialla West is currently at 2.87 m and rising, below the minor flood level. 
  • The Seven Creeks at Kialla West may exceed the minor flood level and may peak near 4.50 metres Monday evening. 
  • The Seven Creeks may reach around the Moderate flood level (5.00 metres) Tuesday morning.
Stay safe - avoid the flooded area. Be aware of potential hazards caused by flooding and never enter floodwater.
What you should do:
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
  • Rising floodwater can be dangerous. Be aware of water levels rising near you.
  • Contact family members and neighbours to ensure they are aware of the situation.
  • Farmers should move livestock and machinery to higher ground if still safe to do.
  • Monitor weather forecasts and river levels. Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/
  • If you are camping close to a creek or river, you may be at risk of flooding and need to move to higher ground, away from waterways.
If you choose to leave:
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications.
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding.
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace.
  • Be aware of any road closures when you leave.
If you are travelling:
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around a find a safe alternative route.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave:
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated.
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow.
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.

Impacts in your area:

At the Seven Creeks at Euroa:

At 2.5 metres (Minor Flood Level)
  • Seven Creeks begins to breakout from its main channel and flows into the surrounding park areas such as the Euroa Caravan Park and Rotary Park.
  • Parkland opposite the Memorial Oval and the Bowls Club (at the corner of Turnbull and Templeton Streets) may start to be inundated.  

At 4.0 metres (Moderate Flood Level)
  • Floodwaters continue to encroach on areas next to the Creek. 
  • Factory Road begins to flood.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

  • Be aware that heavy rainfall may also increase the potential for landslides and debris across roads.
  • Be aware that in fire affected areas, rainfall run-off into waterways may contain debris such as ash, soil, trees and rocks.

  • Follow your emergency plan, if you have one. 
  • Contact family members and neighbours to ensure they are aware of the situation, if safe to do so.

  • Seek shelter indoors, away from floodwater.

This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the Broken River to Benalla.

The Broken River at Benalla is rising rapidly. The Broken River may reach the moderate flood level of 3.70 metres during Monday afternoon. 

Rainfall across the Broken River catchments since Sunday has resulted river level rises and minor flooding. 

Rainfall is forecast to continue for the reminder of Monday into Tuesday, which may result in further river level rises and areas of flooding along the Broken River.
Prepare for moderate flooding in Benalla now. Take actions to protect your life and property against potential hazards caused by flooding. 
What you should do:
  • People and businesses in riverside areas should locate the emergency kits and follow their emergency plans now. 
  • Floodwater is dangerous. Never enter floodwater. 
If you choose to leave:
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications.
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding.
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace.
  • Be aware of any road closures when you leave.
If you are travelling:
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around a find a safe alternative route.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave:
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated.
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow.
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.
Impacts in your area:
  • Floodwater likely to cover Bridge Street near the Botanical Gardens and the Bridge may be closed until the flood peak has passed.
  • Floodwater may threaten the Basketball Pavillion and CFA Fire Station, pump track and skate park.
